brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — IQVIA Predictive Clinical Development Messaging

questions.question: According to the course, what was the composite median R&D program duration in 2016 and 2025?
choices: 6 years in 2016, 8 years in 2025
8 years in 2016, 10 years in 2025
10 years in 2016, 12 years in 2025
7 years in 2016, 9 years in 2025
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—this key data point from Citeline Pharmapremia and the IQVIA Institute is the foundation of the burning platform.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The slide shows R&D duration grew from 8 years to 10 years over that period. This is published benchmark data you can cite by name in sponsor meetings.

questions.question: How long is the Early Engagement framework designed to run?
choices: 6 to 8 weeks
8 to 10 weeks
11 to 12 weeks
14 to 16 weeks
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the 11-to-12-week Early Engagement framework is your entry point and the close of the first conversation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Early Engagement runs for 11 to 12 weeks and produces four concrete artifacts: feasibility view, endpoint tradeoff matrix, country scenario models, and a risk register.

questions.question: What is the correct way to state IQVIA's primary timeline acceleration claim?
choices: IQVIA Predictive Clinical Development guarantees two years off any 10-year program
IQVIA Predictive Clinical Development can deliver up to two years off a 10-year program, with actual timelines varying based on program-specific factors and adoption of IQVIA-recommended approaches
IQVIA Predictive Clinical Development typically saves one to two years
IQVIA Predictive Clinical Development delivers two years off a program on average
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—every word matters in this claim, especially the qualifier and the conditions that make the outcome achievable.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The headline claim requires three essential elements: 'up to two years' (not guaranteed), program-specific factor variation, and adoption of IQVIA-recommended delivery approaches. Overstating this creates expectations IQVIA cannot meet.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four concrete deliverables a sponsor walks away with after Early Engagement?
choices: Feasibility view and endpoint tradeoff matrix
Country scenario models and risk register
Full Clinical Study Report draft
Shared decision log
questions.feedback_correct: Right—the five actual deliverables are feasibility view, endpoint tradeoff matrix, country scenario models, risk register, and shared decision log. The CSR comes much later in Close Out.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Early Engagement produces five specific artifacts you should be able to describe without looking at anything. The Clinical Study Report is a Close Out deliverable, not an Early Engagement output.

questions.question: What percentage faster is site contract negotiation and finalization under IQVIA's accelerated approach?
choices: 18 percent faster
25 percent faster
37 percent faster
33 percent faster
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—site contract negotiation is 18 percent faster (9 weeks versus 11 weeks), and you should always apply the qualifier that these figures are feasible under defined assumptions.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The metrics vary by activity: optimized site selection is 37% faster, country ICF adaptations are 25% faster, lab readiness is greater than 25% faster, and site contract negotiation is specifically 18% faster.

questions.question: According to the course, what does the data ecosystem enable in terms of database lock timing?
choices: Database lock within 30 days
Database lock under 14 days
Database lock within 21 days
Database lock within 8 weeks
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—database lock under 14 days is driven by 81% faster data entry at sites and greater than 50% faster data cleaning.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Close Out phase achieves database lock under 14 days through the data ecosystem's continuous real-time data cleaning and automated issue generation. This is a concrete operational outcome you can cite.

questions.question: What are the six requirements you must verify before representing the accelerated timeline outcomes to a sponsor?
choices: Only the sponsor's willingness to pay and budget approval are needed
Early engagement timing, full-service outsourcing model, protocol optimization, regulatory strategy adoption, collaborative implementation, and ongoing governance
The sponsor only needs to have an approved protocol and IND status
Budget approval, existing vendor relationships, and internal biostatistics capability
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—these six requirements ensure the sponsor can actually achieve the outcomes, and skipping this qualification is both a commercial and ethical risk.
questions.feedback_incorrect: If a sponsor cannot meet all six requirements—including engaging at the pre-IND stage, deploying full-service outsourcing, adopting IQVIA processes and technology, collaborative implementation, and ongoing governance alignment—you should not represent the timeline outcomes as achievable.

questions.question: How should you respond if a sponsor says 'We have already started our trial—can you still help?' based on the course framework?
choices: Tell them it is too late and IQVIA cannot add value once trials are underway
Immediately offer the full two-year acceleration promise regardless of phase
Assess which phase they are in and determine if the six requirements can still be met; recognize that some tools still add real value even if the program is already moving
Insist they start over with IQVIA at protocol stage or nothing can be done
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—this is the right response framework for a realistic objection that comes up in nearly every conversation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course teaches you to assess, not retreat. Which phase are they in? Can the six requirements still be met from here? Early Engagement is the clearest on-ramp, but start-up and conduct-phase tools still add real value even if the program is already moving.

questions.question: When presenting proof points to a sponsor, what discipline does the course emphasize?
choices: Lead with all available proof points to show the breadth of IQVIA's capabilities
Use only AI-related proof points since those differentiate IQVIA most clearly
Select two or three proof points that match the sponsor's specific pain, not all of them
Always open with site satisfaction metrics since those are most credible
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—strategic selection based on sponsor pain is more powerful than overwhelming them with every metric you have.
questions.feedback_incorrect: You have strong proof points available (95% of sites would work with IQVIA again, 53% reduction in screen failures, 35% faster CSR narratives, etc.), but the discipline is in the selection, not the volume. A sponsor worried about enrollment needs different proof points than one focused on regulatory submission timelines.

questions.question: In a first conversation with a Large Pharma Head of Portfolio Operations, what message frame should you emphasize compared to an Emerging Biopharma VP of Development?
choices: Emphasize speed to proof of concept and investor risk reduction for both personas
Emphasize portfolio performance at scale, de-risking before delays, improving global consistency, and supplementing in-house capabilities without replacing them
Emphasize capability replacement and reduction of internal staff needs
Use the exact same message regardless of sponsor type since the solution is identical
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—while the solution is the same, the conversation shifts dramatically based on sponsor type and what matters most to their business.
questions.feedback_incorrect: For Large and Mid Pharma, the message centers on portfolio performance at scale, de-risking before delays occur, and supplementing (not replacing) in-house capabilities. For Emerging Biopharma, the focus is on speed to proof of concept and reducing investor and governance risk. Persona alignment is essential to credibility.
